list: The official 55 trophies as PlayStation publishes them; kinds, stages, missable flags, guides and sources are this atlas's own work.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide:
The platinum, and the whole point of this atlas: it unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for it directly.

Work the roadmap in order — story first (watching the seven missables), then the collectible sweep, then the activity grind, then clean-up and 100% completion. If your tracker shows 54 of 55 with only this one greyed out, you are one trophy from done: check the grade tallies at the top of the tracker to see which grade is short.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the campaign. It is unmissable and pops at the mission's end card, whatever difficulty or choices you play with.

Take the mission slowly: it doubles as the game's tutorial for moving between the two protagonists and for the partner system that several later feats (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) depend on. Everything it teaches comes back, so do not skip its prompts.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for completing Chapter 1. Unmissable: it pops when the chapter's last mission wraps up and the Chapter 2 title card appears.

Before you push into Chapter 2, clear any strand missions already on your map (Andy's strand opens early). Strands are the missable risk in this list — see the Missables view — and Chapter 1 is the cheapest time to keep them current.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for completing Chapter 2 — yes, the name really is published with the asterisks. Unmissable, awarded at the chapter's closing mission.

Chapter 2 opens up more of Leonida and the first big set-piece missions (Breakfast Run and The Cartel Heist sit in this stretch). Keep an eye on the meditation spots and WAiNK locations in each new area as you pass through: collecting as you go turns the Stage 2 sweep into a short mop-up instead of a full tour.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for completing Chapter 3, the midpoint of the campaign. Unmissable.

By now every strand character has appeared. The strand finales for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone are this atlas's main missables: their final missions must be finished before the endgame locks the story down, so if a strand icon is sitting on your map at the Chapter 3 break, do it before the next main mission.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for completing Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale sequence. Unmissable.

Treat the end of Chapter 4 as the soft point of no return: finish every open character strand and any meditation spots that sit in story locations before you start the final mission. Everything else on the list — collectibles, activities, feats — stays available in free roam afterwards.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide:
The gold story trophy, for completing the final mission of the campaign. Unmissable once started, and the credits roll straight into free roam, so nothing about finishing the story locks you out of the rest of the list — except the missables flagged in this atlas.

Before you start it: clear the five strand finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), because their characters' stories end here. Bring full ammo, armour and snacks; the finale is the longest combat stretch in the game, and dying only costs you a checkpoint restart.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for the named mission Breakfast Run. Unmissable — it is a main-path mission, and the trophy pops on completion regardless of how messy the run gets.

Breakfast Run is an early driving-and-delivery mission: the clock matters more than combat, so take the marked route, use the partner's directions, and do not stop to fight anyone who is not blocking the road. If you fail a leg, the checkpoint restarts are generous.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for The Cartel Heist, the campaign's first full heist. Unmissable and awarded on completion, whichever approach the mission offers you.

The heist is a template for the robbery feats later in the list (Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play): watch how the game handles alarm states, loot timers and the escape, because the same rules apply in free roam. Take the louder approach on a first playthrough — it teaches the police response you will be escaping from for the rest of the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for the named mission Child's Play. Unmissable, on the main path.

This is one of the quieter character missions — mostly driving and conversation rather than gunplay. It cannot be failed in a way that costs the trophy, so relax and let it play out; the choices you make in it feed the running total behind Actions Speak Louder.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for the named mission Headliners. Unmissable.

Headliners is a public-spectacle mission with crowds and cameras around, so keep your wanted level down until the scripted moment: drawing police attention early only makes the scripted escape longer. Follow the objective markers, use the vehicle provided, and the trophy pops at the mission's end.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. Unmissable.

Remember this location: VCIA is where Catch Me If You Can (an unscheduled departure) is earned in free roam, and the takedown teaches you the airport's layout, service roads and fences. During the mission, note the hangar and perimeter roads — you will come back for them in Stage 4 clean-up.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide:
Story trophy for Operation Savage Glory, the campaign's big military-style set piece. Unmissable.

This mission puts heavy armour and vehicles on the field — the closest the story comes to the Rhino tanks behind Challenging Tank. Learn how the game wants you to deal with armour here (explosives, flanking, stealing the vehicle) while the checkpoints are kind, rather than in free roam with a wanted level attached.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide:
The second gold: reach 100% on the game's completion counter. This is not the same as the platinum — 100% tracks the game's own checklist (story, strands, collectibles, activities and a slice of the feats), and the counter in the pause menu is the source of truth.

Work it last, in Stage 4, and chase the counter category by category: whatever sits below 100% in a category names your next job. Most players finish with collectibles and challenges outstanding, so use this tracker's counters — stunts, cards, WAiNK spots, challenges — to find the gap instead of guessing.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide:
Complete 250 stunts — the jumps, flips and near-miss feats the game scores as stunts, tracked by the counter on this trophy. Any stunt the game registers counts, and repeats count, so this is a volume trophy rather than a skill wall.

The fastest farming is a fast car or bike on the airport and causeway stretches: long straights, ramps and traffic to thread for near-miss bonuses. Work in sessions and log your count here after each one; 250 arrives sooner than it looks if you take stunt-friendly routes whenever you cross the map for other trophies.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide:
Try each type of activity once — all 9 activity types on the map: races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, bowling, stunts, challenges and hunting. You only have to start each one, not win it.

Do this early in Stage 3: it is a tour of everything the grind stages need, and several types (the range, the drone races) are trophies in their own right at higher targets. Tick each type off as you sample it and the trophy pops on the ninth.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide:
Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges. The range runs weapon-class sets — pistols, SMGs, rifles, shotguns and more — and each challenge is scored on hits and accuracy against a gold threshold, so this is the list's purest aim test.

Learn one set at a time and replay until the medal sticks before moving on; the tracker counter here (x/42) is the reliable record, since the range menu buries your medals per weapon. Sensitivity and aim-assist settings are fair game — set them for the range and change them back outside. If a gold feels impossible, its threshold usually rewards accuracy over speed: slow down and stop dropping shots.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide:
Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations. A win means first place at that location once; the same course can be retried immediately, and the drone handling is identical everywhere, so your lap times improve as you go.

Start with the open coastal courses to learn the gates, then take the city courses where the line threads between buildings. Log each location win in the counter (x/14) — with 14 scattered across Leonida, the tracker is how you avoid re-flying a course you already won.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide:
Win 20 different races — different is the operative word: replaying one race 20 times does nothing. Any race type on land counts, and there are more than 20 on the map, so you can skip the ones whose vehicle class you hate.

Bring the best vehicle you own for each class and upgrade it before the series, not during. Log wins in the counter as you go (x/20) and mark which races are done; the map does not make won-once races easy to tell apart later.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide:
Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing contact whose challenge events appear at the piers and lakes on the map; enter one and finish with a better catch score than his when the timer ends.

The challenge is scored on the fish you actually land, so keep the line tension in the green and do not rush the reel — a lost big fish costs more than a slow small one. If Cal wins a round, the challenge can be re-entered straight away; his score varies, and most players take him within a few attempts once the reeling rhythm clicks.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide:
Complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet in Leonida. 'Complete' means finishing the cabinet's game — reaching its end or final score screen — not just playing a credit.

Pick the shortest cabinet you can find; the trophy does not care which game or how well you score, only that you finish it. Arcades sit in the Vice City entertainment districts and at least one is near the Ocean Beach strip, so you can knock this out during Stage 2's sweep.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableNote: Andy's strand closes when he leaves Leonida partway through the story. If his final mission is not done before then, the strand is gone for the rest of the playthrough — finish Andy's missions as they appear, and clear the strand before the end of Chapter 4 at the very latest.
trophies.guide:
Complete the final mission of Andy's strand — the chain of missions Andy gives you, ending with his finale. The trophy pops when that last mission ends, not before, so a strand that looks finished but never showed its final mission is not done.

Play Andy's missions in order as they unlock and do not let them queue up behind the main story: this strand is missable (see the warning above), and the safe habit for all five strand characters is the same — a strand icon on the map outranks a main mission. PowerPyx's and PSNProfiles' strand orders both put Andy's finale well before the endgame if you keep up.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableNote: Kenton's strand is tied to the waterfront, and his final mission stops being offered once the story moves past his part in it. Finish Kenton's chain before the finale sequence begins; a Kenton icon left on the map at that point is a trophy lost for this playthrough.
trophies.guide:
Complete the final mission of Kenton's strand. Kenton's missions run around the marinas and the working waterfront — expect boat legs and dockside fights rather than highway chases.

Like every strand finale here it is missable, so treat Kenton's icon as urgent whenever it appears. Do the strand in one or two sittings: the missions chain into each other, the finale unlocks straight after the penultimate one, and the trophy pops at its end card.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableNote: Billy rides out of the story for good at a set point, and his final mission goes with him. Complete Billy's strand before starting the final mission — it is one of the five strand finales this atlas flags, and there is no post-story way back to it.
trophies.guide:
Complete the final mission of Billy's strand. Billy's chain is road-heavy — long rides and vehicle work across the state's highways — and its finale is the last of his missions to unlock.

This trophy is hidden on PlayStation and missable in play: Billy's strand closes when he leaves, so keep his missions current as the story advances. If you are reading this in the tracker with the spoiler shield on, the trophy is a story trophy — earn it in Stage 1, not in clean-up.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. A strand counts when its whole chain is finished — the named characters (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of them, and Bret's hunting and the other stranger chains make up the rest.

The five named strands are missable, so they are both the risk and the shortcut: finish them in Stage 1 and you are five-eighths of the way here. The counter (x/8) tracks completed strands, not missions — a strand only ticks when its final mission ends.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableNote: Randy's supply operation is shut down by story events, and his final mission is only offered while it runs. Keep Randy's strand current through the middle chapters — if it is still open when the endgame starts, it will not survive it.
trophies.guide:
Complete the final mission of Randy's strand. Randy's chain is about moving product — expect timed deliveries and escort legs where the cargo matters more than the shooting.

Missable, like all five strand finales: play Randy's missions as they unlock rather than banking them. The trophy pops at the finale's end; if you have done the strand and it has not popped, you have a mission left — strands always end with an explicit final mission.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableNote: Tyrone's strand ends when his story does, partway through the campaign's later chapters. His final mission must be completed before the finale sequence; afterwards Tyrone is gone and so is the trophy for this run.
trophies.guide:
Complete the final mission of Tyrone's strand — the last of the five named strand finales in this atlas. Tyrone's missions lean into vehicle set pieces, so keep a fast, durable car as your active vehicle while you run his chain.

Missable: finish Tyrone's strand before the endgame. Together with Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy, his finale is one of the five strand trophies that decide whether a playthrough can still reach the platinum without a replay.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: Flagged missable by PowerPyx: some of the 18 meditation spots sit in places the story changes or locks as it advances, so a spot skipped early can be unreachable later. Meditate at each spot the first time you reach its area instead of saving them all for clean-up.
trophies.guide:
Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Each spot is a marked place — a viewpoint, a shoreline, a quiet rooftop — where you stop and run the short meditation interaction; the counter here tracks them (x/18).

PowerPyx flags this trophy as the list's one missable collectible: a few spots are tied to locations the story alters, so the safe play is to meditate whenever you first reach a spot's area during the story, then sweep whatever is left in Stage 2. PSNProfiles' and PlayStationTrophies.org's spot lists group them by region, which matches the sweep order in this atlas's roadmap.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableNote: The unique animal is a single scripted encounter in Bret's hunting strand — it is not a random spawn. If Bret's strand is left unfinished when the story moves on, or the encounter is abandoned mid-hunt, there is no second chance in the same playthrough: take the hunt when Bret offers it and see it through.
trophies.guide:
Hunt the unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunting strand builds through ordinary hunts and ends with one unique animal — a specific, named encounter rather than a species you can find anywhere.

Go in prepared: the right weapon for the animal's size, a full health bar, and patience on the tracking leg, because spooking it drags the hunt out. The trophy pops when the unique animal is down and the strand's closing scene plays. Because the encounter is one-off (see the missable warning), do not start it half-equipped and quit out.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide:
Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are found one at a time across Leonida — on counters, in bars, at viewpoints — and each set is complete only when every card in it is collected, so the counter (x/3) moves slowly and then all at once.

Work set by set, not card by card: finish the set you are closest to before starting another. GTA Zone's and PowerPyx's card maps group the cards by set and region; sweep a region for all its cards in one pass during Stage 2 rather than crossing the map for singles.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide:
Use a WAiNK point at 100 locations. WAiNK points are the branded interaction spots scattered over the state — each one counts once, the first time you use it, and the counter (x/100) is the only sane way to keep track.

There are more than 100 in the world, so you have slack for any that are awkward to reach. Fold them into everything else: WAiNK points cluster in the same commercial areas as shops and cards, so a Stage 2 sweep that does cards, spots and WAiNK points street by street finishes all three together.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide:
Complete 50 Challenges — the short, scored tasks the game offers all over Leonida (time trials, target scores, stunt goals and the like). Any 50 count; the pool is bigger than 50, so you can abandon a challenge type you dislike and still finish.

Challenges unlock as you explore, so this pairs naturally with The Goodtime State's full-map exploration. Log completions in the counter (x/50) as you go — the game counts them, but the tracker is what tells you at a glance whether you are at 31 or 49.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide:
With your partner beside you, earn a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely — the stars must drain to zero with the partner still with you, so no splitting up and no switching away mid-escape.

The reliable method: cause trouble together somewhere with a fast car and a tunnel, underpass or parking structure nearby. At 4 stars, break line of sight, get under cover and wait out the search with the engine off. Rooftops and alley mouths work; open beach does not — helicopters keep the search alive. Do it before the finale if you want it painless, while the partner is freely available in roam.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide:
Rob 3 shops in an unbroken chain with your partner: the wanted level from the first robbery must never fully clear before the third is done. 'Back-to-back' means one continuous heat, so plan the route before you start.

Pick three shops on one commercial street, rob the first, drive — do not hide — to the second, and keep moving to the third. Losing the cops entirely resets the chain, and so does losing your partner, so keep them in the car. A fast four-door and a pre-planned loop of three close shops makes this a two-minute trophy.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide:
Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle is discovered the first time you get in and drive it, and the counter (x/100) tracks distinct models, not total cars stolen.

You will pass 60 without trying just by playing. For the rest, work the rich districts and the airport: high-end models park up in Vice Beach and the marina districts, working trucks and vans live in the port and industrial areas, and every story mission tends to hand you something new. If it has a steering wheel and you have not sat in it, sit in it.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide:
Take down 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus, the slow-time aiming ability. All five must fall before the meter ends — wounding does not count, and kills after it expires do not either.

Set it up somewhere enemies cluster: a gang operation, a police standoff at low stars, or a story shootout replay. Line up five targets at mid-range, use a high-capacity weapon, trigger Focus and work left to right without re-aiming from scratch — headshots keep the streak fast enough to fit inside the meter.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide:
Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport: get airborne in a plane you were never cleared to take. In practice: enter the airfield in free roam, take one of the parked aircraft, and lift off.

You will draw a wanted level for being on the tarmac, so be quick: enter through the service gates you scouted during VCIA Takedown, run straight for the nearest light aircraft, and climb out over the water. The trophy pops once the departure registers — wheels up, not merely rolling.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide:
The vaguest description on the list — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — is about the Rhino tank: get inside one and use it. Rhinos appear at high wanted levels and in military hands; the trophy is for taking one over and putting it to work, not just seeing one.

The controlled way is to draw a Rhino out at a high wanted level somewhere with cover, kill its escort from range, and take the hatch while its driver is dealt with — explosives and sticky bombs clear the area without destroying the tank itself. Operation Savage Glory in the story is your rehearsal for how Rhinos behave.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide:
Rob a jewelry store with zero detection: no alarm raised, no witness completing a call, no wanted level. Detection is the whole trophy — the take itself can be small.

Go at night, masked, and take the store's staff down quietly before anyone reaches a phone or the counter alarm; a suppressed weapon or melee takedowns keep it silent. Plan the exit before you enter: if the street outside is empty and your car faces out, you can be gone before the first patrol would ever know. If you are detected, leave and let the heat die — the store can be robbed again later.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide:
Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — each one only counts when you get away, so the counter (x/5) is really five successful escapes, not five attempts. Vault robberies are the heavy end of free-roam crime: forced entry, a timed loot, and a serious police response.

Treat each like a mini-heist: scout the escape route first, park the getaway car facing out, loot fast and leave on the timer rather than greedily. The Cartel Heist in the story teaches the rhythm. Spread the five across different banks — a bank you just hit is the worst one to revisit while its heat is fresh.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide:
Rob an armoured truck and escape with the take. Armoured trucks run routes in free roam; the rear doors are the way in — they need to be blown or forced, which means explosives and an immediate wanted level.

Hit the truck somewhere your escape is short: near a tunnel mouth, a multi-storey car park or the underpass network. Blow the doors, grab the cash, and be moving before the response converges. One clean truck is all the trophy asks for.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide:
Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — every named district and region on the map must be visited at least once, and the counter (x/52) ticks as each new area registers.

Most areas open up just by doing everything else in this atlas. The stragglers are always the same kind: small islands, the far swamp edges and districts no mission visits. Late in Stage 2, compare your map against GTA Zone's area map, pick the grey patches, and take a boat or plane to whatever is left.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide:
Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — one operation per gang, and the counter (x/9) tracks gangs hit, not operations robbed. Hitting the same gang twice does nothing for this trophy.

Operations are marked by gang territory: learn each gang's colours and ground from the map, rob one site cleanly, and move to a different gang's turf for the next. Keep a list here as you go — by the seventh gang, nobody remembers which two are left without one.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide:
Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — the throwback trophy of the list, a nod to where the series' Vice City story began. In play it is simple: at the Ocean Beach strip, order a cocktail at a beachfront bar and drink it where you can see the water.

If it does not pop at the first bar, try the hotel bars along the beachfront rather than inland clubs — the 'with a view' part is literal, and the terrace spots facing the ocean are the ones that register. A daytime visit makes the right spots easy to spot.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide:
Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: steal a car inside a showroom and drive it out through the glass. The showroom must be entered on foot — the trophy wants the full sequence, in the door and out through the window in their car.

The premium showrooms in the Vice Beach and downtown districts are the spots. Pick the car nearest the glass, already facing it if you can, and go: the smash registers the moment you break through, and the wanted level that follows is just the price of the exit.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide:
Play a game at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and finish with a follow-through — the alley is a named location, not any bowling minigame spot, and the trophy is tied to playing there properly.

Find the alley, start a game and play it out to the end of the tenth frame; the follow-through is part of the standard bowling animation when you bowl a full game rather than quitting mid-way. This also ticks bowling off the activity list for Master of None if you have not bowled yet.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide:
'A partnership with mass appeal' is the partner system showing off: this one is earned through the two protagonists working together in public — taking on an activity or feat as a pair and finishing it with an audience, in the game's social sense.

The dependable route is to run partner activities in the busiest districts (Ocean Beach, the boardwalk, downtown) and finish them cleanly together rather than solo: pair up, pick a public activity, complete it as the pair. Players report it popping during ordinary paired play in crowded areas, so if you do the other partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) in populated spots, expect this one along the way.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide:
Choices made, for better or worse: PlayStation tracks this trophy with a counter that runs to 500, and the choices it counts are the small decisions the game logs constantly — dialogue picks, spare-or-kill calls, approach selections, strand outcomes.

There is no farming spot and no need for one: 500 sounds enormous until you realise ordinary play makes dozens of tracked choices an hour. Play the story and strands, answer when the game asks, and check the counter (x/500) now and then — most players find it well advanced by the end of the story and finished during clean-up.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide:
'Second time's the charm' — the trophy for failing at something and then succeeding at the same thing on the retry. The natural reading, and the one players confirm, is an activity or challenge failed once and then completed on the next attempt.

If it has not popped on its own, manufacture it: enter a short race or challenge, fail it deliberately, immediately re-enter and win. Keep the two attempts back-to-back at the same event so the game reads them as a pair.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide:
Witness something strange — Leonida's weird-encounter trophy. Out in the swamps and the far edges of the map, the game hides unexplained events: lights, creatures, things the characters comment on and the game never explains.

These encounters are placed, not random: they wait at specific spots, mostly at night, mostly far from the city. Exploration for The Goodtime State takes you past most of their ground — when the music changes and your character reacts to something that is not an enemy, stop and watch it play out. Watching to the end is what registers.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide:
Knock a pedestrian down with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, strike someone with a melee weapon out of the window/side as you pass. It has to be the melee hit from the vehicle that bowls them over — running them down with the bumper does not count.

A motorcycle or an open car makes the swing easiest. Find a lone pedestrian on a quiet street, line up a slow pass, and swing as you draw level: too fast and you just clip them with the vehicle, too slow and they step away. One clean knockdown is the whole trophy.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide:
Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies — vaults, trucks and operations pay partly in marked money — and laundering is done through the contact option that converts them at a cut.

This is a cumulative money total, and it pairs with Maximum Withdrawal and Pest Control: the same robberies that fill those counters fill this one. Do not sell marked bills short through quick options if any are offered; the trophy counts what passes through your laundering contacts specifically, so route every marked stack that way until the total lands.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide:
Spend $100,000 across all shops — every till in Leonida counts: clothes, weapons, vehicle work, property services, all of it. It is a lifetime spend total, not a single spree.

You will spend a good share of it without noticing while upgrading cars and restocking between missions. If you finish the story short of the mark, the fastest honest route is vehicle customisation: full performance and cosmetic builds on a few kept cars burn money quickly and leave you with something to show for it.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide:
Purchase all 8 garage properties on the map. Garages are bought at their for-sale signs; the counter (x/8) tracks purchases, and the set spans the state from city lock-ups to rural barns.

Buy them as your money allows during the story rather than in one end-game sweep — they are useful storage the whole game, and their prices are fixed, so there is no saving to wait for. The last one or two are usually the remote ones no mission passes; GTA Zone's property map pins all eight.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide:
Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-phone service that keeps vehicles for you. Registering is done from the phone while you are in or beside a vehicle you want kept; the counter (x/10) tracks registrations.

Register the keepers as you find them — the fast car, the good bike, the boat-adjacent truck — instead of grinding ten at the end. Any ten distinct vehicles finish it, and it pairs with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you sit in for discovery is a registration candidate.
